what_happened: Root cause of the C16 finding located: LadderChain.lean:2135 carries 'set_option linter.unusedVariables false in', which silences only the FRONTEND linter. The C16 finding comes from Batteries' @[env_linter] unusedArguments, a different linter that set_option does not reach. Task 850 silenced one and missed the other.

The dispatch's 'remove hslk from the signature' option is not available: mem_cellAt_of_shift_of_hasForwardSlack is a PINNED Challenge statement (specs/849_.../challenge/manifest.json and that plan's '## Lean Challenge Statements' block, where hslk appears verbatim). Removing the binder would be the signature drift plan-compliance.md's Statement Fidelity section forbids. Decision routed to the exemption branch instead.

The round-1 research report settled the disposition (hand-inserted scripts/nolints.json row plus a repaired reason comment) with all three alternatives rejected on their merits and the exact covering commands named, so planning needed no second research round and no user decision; the plan is a direct transcription of its Recommendations section.

The stale '217 findings' header comments in scripts/check-module-invariants.sh (two occurrences, now understating a live 227 rows) are a known advisory-only defect the research flagged as optionally repairable in this task's commit, but that file sits inside concurrent sibling task 860's declared file_scope this cycle. Excluded from the plan's scope and recorded in Non-Goals rather than contending for the file; no check reads those comments.

Phase 1's comment-only edit added 11 net lines to LadderChain.lean, which drifted typst/generated/status.typ's formalsystem-line-count (388946 -> 388957) and the typst-sync-check.sh Check 2 pre-commit hook BLOCKED the phase commit. The drift was self-caused and exactly accounted for (+11), verified by confirming LadderChain.lean was the only uncommitted .lean under FormalSystem/, so --no-verify was NOT used. Remedy: full guarded lake build, then 'bash scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix', then stage typst/generated/status.typ alongside LadderChain.lean. This widens the phase's staging set beyond the plan's declared single file: ANY net line-count change to a .lean file drags typst/generated/status.typ into the same commit, a coupling the plan did not anticipate.

check-module-invariants.sh reported PASS C16 (the task's objective) but still exited 1 on a DIFFERENT group: 'FAIL INV 3 file(s) carry a stale generated inventory block' naming FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/RaySummary/README.md, FormalSystem/Metalogic/README.md and README.md. The plan's risk table anticipated these exact three README surfaces as concurrent sibling 860's territory and directed that such a failure be reported, not repaired. Measurement overturned that attribution: the inventory blocks record per-file LINE COUNTS (LadderChain.lean recorded at 2,216, live 2,227), so the staleness is the +11-line Phase 1 comment edit cascading up three aggregator READMEs. Task 860 is 'completed' in state.json, not live; the only contention manifest on disk is from an unrelated October session and names only docs/theorem-index.md for tasks 705/710; and git status shows no uncommitted README edits. Repaired with 'bash scripts/check-module-invariants.sh --emit-inventory'. The transferable lesson: in this repo ANY net line-count change to a .lean file fans out to typst/generated/status.typ AND every aggregator README inventory block above it, so a 'comment-only, one file' Lean edit is never a one-file commit.

The plan's Scope Hypotheses held exactly, with zero re-derivation cost: the reason comment at LadderChain.lean:2132-2134, set_option at 2135, theorem at 2142, scripts/nolints.json at 227 rows all of category unusedArguments, and check-module-invariants.sh as its only real consumer (the four other scripts/ grep hits are prose mentions only). The fully-qualified name the research report captured from the linter's own output was reusable verbatim, so no baseline runLinter run was needed to confirm spelling -- 'section DelNxtIter' is a section rather than a namespace, so the name carries no DelNxtIter segment. Both substantive edits landed first-try and runLinter went green on the first attempt.
